chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from 'Ali from Abi Basir said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about going out (traveling) when Ramadan enters, so he said: 'No, except in what I inform you of: going out to Mecca, or a campaign in the way of Allah, or wealth whose destruction you fear, or a brother whose destruction you fear.' And he said: 'Indeed, he is not a brother from the father and the mother.'

key_terms.أَخًا مِنَ الْأَبِ وَالْأُمِّ: A brother from father and mother (full sibling)

ai.seo_question: What are the valid reasons for traveling during Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the specific exemptions for traveling during Ramadan, emphasizing that mere kinship is insufficient unless it involves a full sibling (*akh*) whose preservation is at stake. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between general relatives and the specific bond of full siblings, prioritizing the protection of life and wealth as valid grounds for breaking the fast. The clarification underscores the practical application of *darura* (necessity) within the framework of Ramadan obligations.
